# Reading Wꜣḏyt the way it was meant to be written
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Wꜣḏyt** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Wadjet's mythology is woven into kingship from the first dynasties. She does not have a single epic cycle; she has a thousand crowns, amulets, and royal names. From the First Dynasty, the royal titulary includes the name of the Two Ladies, Nekhbet and Wadjet.  The vulture and the cobra together guard Upper and Lower Egypt; their union is the political theology of the unified kingdom.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Wꜣḏyt
- **ASCII form:** wadjet
- **Meaning:** "The green one"
- **Domain of influence:** Cobra, Protection, Lower Egypt
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𓇅𓏏𓆗
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 261 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Wꜣḏyt** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *wadjet* and **Wꜣḏyt** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Wꜣḏyt** lives at [/sites/wadjet/](/sites/wadjet/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/wadjet/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/wadjet/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/wadjet/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Wꜣḏyt** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Insurance & Protection Services** — The cobra on the crown; protection as sovereign promise.
- **Beauty, Fashion & Cosmetics** — Malachite eye paint was her sacrament; protective cosmetics began under her color.
- **Gems, Jewelry & Luxury Materials** — The wedjat-eye amulet — among the most worn protective jewels in human history.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Egyptian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/wadjet/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
